subject: Cloud Computing
title: Vendor Lock-In Tactics
description: A quick win: understand Vendor Lock-In Tactics.

hook.text: Cloud providers want you to stay forever. Every proprietary service is a thread that ties you tighter.

buildup.text: AWS Lambda, Azure Active Directory, and Google BigQuery all have no direct equivalent on other clouds.

discovery.text: Data egress charges punish leaving. Moving a petabyte out of AWS costs roughly $90,000.

twist.text: Some lock-in is worth it. Proprietary services are often better than generic alternatives.

climax.text: The key is choosing lock-in deliberately — knowing the cost of leaving before you commit.

punchline.text: Lock-in isn't always bad. Accidental lock-in always is.

quiz.question: How do data egress charges contribute to cloud lock-in?
options: They make moving data out of a provider extremely expensive
They charge extra for uploading data to the cloud
They limit the amount of data you can store

details.summary: Cloud providers create lock-in through proprietary services, data egress fees, proprietary APIs, training investments, and ecosystem advantages. While each tactic has legitimate technical value, they collectively make switching providers extremely expensive and time-consuming.
details.whyItMatters: Lock-in is the biggest strategic risk in cloud computing. Recognizing lock-in mechanisms helps organizations make conscious choices about which dependencies they accept.
takeaways: Proprietary services create the deepest technical lock-in
Data egress fees make moving data out expensive
Team expertise and training create practical switching costs

faq.question: How can lock-in be minimized?
faq.answer: Use open-source and standard technologies like Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, and Terraform. Containerize applications for portability. Abstract provider-specific services behind interfaces. Accept some lock-in where the value of managed services outweighs the switching cost.

faq.question: Is all lock-in bad in practice?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Proprietary managed services often provide significant developer productivity and operational benefits. The key is making conscious decisions: accept lock-in where the value is clear, and avoid it for core business logic that might need to move later.
